decisions.reason: As in 2:11: the setting is on the noun, and the pronouns that refer back to it are generic French in both options. Balanced says "une personne" and Readable "les gens", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: examiner (L); juger, évaluer (B) (for the whole book; 2:15, 4:3-4)
decisions.reason: The Corinthians term sheet keeps "examine" at Literal, so that the courtroom sense can come through in chapter 4; Balanced says what the examining is for, weighing rightly (m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:el ser humano natural|el hombre natural}}; para él, no span
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting for the noun. Both options are masculine words, so "para él" agrees with either and needs no span; the English needs spans on its pronouns as well.

decisions.choice: se examinan (L); evaluar (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for examining and judging in 2:15 and 4:3-4. Literal says "examinar" each time; Balanced says "evaluar" here and in 2:15, where the sense is weighing something rightly, and keeps the courtroom words in chapter 4.

decisions.choice: mtu wa asili (L); mtu aliye na uhai wa asili tu (B); watu wasio na Roho wa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision: someone with only ordinary human life, without God's Spirit. "Kidunia" (worldly) would blur this word with "ulimwengu" (world).

decisions.choice: kuchunguza (L); kupima (B)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice for this Greek verb (2:14–15; 4:3–4): Literal always "kuchunguza" (examine); Balanced "kupima" (weigh, assess) here, and the courtroom sense in chapter 4.

decisions.choice: "người tự nhiên" (L); "người chỉ có sự sống tự nhiên" (B); "những người không có Thánh Linh của Đức Chúa Trời" (R) for psychikos anthropos; "tự nhiên" kept for psychikos in 15:44-46
decisions.reason: The word is built on psyche, natural human life. "Tự nhiên" (natural) is set against "thuộc linh" (spiritual), the pair of 15:44-46; "xác thịt" is kept for sarx (3:1-3) so the two Greek words stay apart. "Người", "người ấy" need no gender span.

decisions.choice: "được xem xét" (L); "đánh giá ... cho đúng" (B) for anakrino (also 2:15)
decisions.reason: "Xét đoán" is kept for krino (judge, condemn), as in Romans 14; anakrino is to examine and weigh, the word of the courtroom in 4:3-4.

decisions.choice: "자연적인 사람" (L); "타고난 생명만 가진 사람" (B); "하나님의 영이 없는 사람들" (R), here and for the natural body in 15:44-46 ("자연적인 몸")
decisions.reason: The meaning decision describes a person who has only ordinary human life, without the Spirit. "육에 속한" would blur this word with the flesh (육신) of 3:1-3, which is a different Greek word, so Korean uses "자연적인", the word that answers "영적인" in 15:44.

decisions.choice: "살피다" (L); "판단하다" (B, R) for the verb of verses 14-15, here and in 4:3-4
decisions.reason: The verb means to examine closely, as a judge does at a hearing; Literal keeps "살피다" every time, and Balanced says "판단하다", which also serves the court scene of chapter 4.

source.text: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει τὰ πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπ’ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται.

records.literal_gloss: The however spiritual [one] examines all things, he however by no one is examined.

en.L: But the spiritual [person] examines all things, but {{gender:that person|he himself}} is examined by no one.
en.B: But the spiritual person is able to assess all things, while no one is in a position to assess such a person.
en.R: But people who have the Spirit can judge what is true about everything. And no one without the Spirit is able to judge them.

fr.L: Mais celui qui est spirituel examine tout, et lui-même n’est examiné par personne.
fr.B: Mais celui qui est spirituel peut évaluer toutes choses, et personne n’est en mesure de l’évaluer.
fr.R: Mais ceux qui ont l’Esprit peuvent juger ce qui est vrai en toutes choses. Et ceux qui n’ont pas l’Esprit ne peuvent pas les juger.

sw.L: Lakini mtu wa kiroho huchunguza mambo yote, lakini yeye mwenyewe hachunguzwi na mtu yeyote.
sw.B: Lakini mtu wa kiroho anaweza kupima mambo yote, wakati hakuna mtu aliye na nafasi ya kumpima yeye.
sw.R: Lakini watu walio na Roho wanaweza kuamua kilicho kweli kuhusu kila kitu. Na hakuna mtu asiye na Roho anayeweza kuwahukumu wao.

es.L: Pero el espiritual examina todas las cosas, pero {{gender:esa persona no es examinada|él mismo no es examinado}} por nadie.
es.B: Pero la persona espiritual puede evaluar todas las cosas, mientras que nadie está en condiciones de evaluarla a ella.
es.R: Pero las personas que tienen el Espíritu pueden juzgar lo que es verdad acerca de todo. Y nadie que no tenga el Espíritu puede juzgarlas a ellas.

vi.L: Nhưng người thuộc linh xem xét mọi sự, còn chính người ấy thì không bị ai xem xét.
vi.B: Nhưng người thuộc linh có thể đánh giá mọi sự, còn không ai có tư cách để đánh giá người ấy.
vi.R: Nhưng những người có Thánh Linh có thể nhận định đúng về mọi điều. Và không ai thiếu Thánh Linh lại có thể nhận định về họ.

ko.L: 그러나 영적인 사람은 모든 것을 살피지만, 그 자신은 아무에게도 살핌을 받지 않습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 성령의 사람은 모든 것을 판단할 수 있습니다. 그러나 아무도 그런 사람을 판단할 자리에 있지 않습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 성령을 모신 사람들은 무엇이 참된지 모든 것을 판단할 수 있습니다. 그리고 성령이 없는 사람은 아무도 그들을 판단할 수 없습니다.

decisions.choice: the spiritual person: one who has God's Spirit and is guided by the Spirit
alternatives: a person with unusual spiritual experiences
decisions.reason: πνευματικὸς is the opposite of the natural person in verse 14. In 3:1 Paul says he could not speak to the Corinthians as spiritual people, though they had the Spirit, because they lived by merely human standards: being spiritual shows in how one lives.

decisions.choice: examines all things: can weigh rightly everything that concerns God's gifts and God's ways
decisions.reason: ἀνακρίνει is the verb of verse 14. Paul does not claim that spiritual people know everything; he means that the Spirit enables them to judge rightly the things the natural person cannot (verse 14).

decisions.choice: no one without the Spirit is in a position to pass judgment on a spiritual person
alternatives: spiritual people are answerable to no one at all
decisions.reason: Paul does not put spiritual people beyond correction: he corrects the Corinthians at length, and prophecy is to be weighed (14:29). The point is that a natural person cannot judge the things of the Spirit or those who live by them. In 4:3-4 Paul applies this to the Corinthians' judging of him: the Lord is his judge.

decisions.choice: {{gender:that person|he himself}}
decisions.reason: αὐτὸς refers to the spiritual person, who may be a man or a woman. Balanced says "such a person" and Readable uses the plural, which need no setting.

decisions.choice: no one without the Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit who "no one" refers to (m3). This narrows Paul's general statement and is marked for reviewers.

decisions.choice: celui qui est spirituel ... lui-même (L)
decisions.reason: French "celui qui" is generic and needs no gender setting, where the English needs {{gender:that person|he himself}}. "Le spirituel" alone would read as an abstract noun.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona no es examinada|él mismo no es examinado}}
alternatives: él mismo no es examinado, with no setting
decisions.reason: Spanish follows the English setting. The participle has to agree with "persona" (feminine) or "él" (masculine), so the span takes in the whole clause up to the participle.

decisions.choice: "người thuộc linh" (L, B); "những người có Thánh Linh" (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as "những người thuộc linh" in Galatians 6:1; Readable says plainly what it is, as the English does.

source.text: τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου, ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Who for knew [the] mind of [the] Lord, who will instruct him?

en.L: For "who has known [the] mind of [the] Lord, who will instruct {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: For "who has ever known the mind of the Lord well enough to instruct {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.R: The Scriptures ask, "Who knows what the Lord is thinking? Who can teach {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} anything?"

fr.L: Car « qui a connu la pensée du Seigneur, qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}instruira ? »
fr.B: Car « qui a jamais connu la pensée du Seigneur au point de pouvoir {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}instruire ? »
fr.R: Les Écritures demandent : « Qui sait ce que pense le Seigneur ? Qui peut {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} apprendre quoi que ce soit ? »

sw.L: Kwa maana "ni nani aliyeijua nia ya Bwana, ni nani atakayemfundisha?"
sw.B: Kwa maana "ni nani amewahi kuijua nia ya Bwana kiasi cha kuweza kumfundisha?"
sw.R: Maandiko yanauliza, "Ni nani anayejua Bwana anafikiri nini? Ni nani anayeweza kumfundisha {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} jambo lolote?"

es.L: Porque «¿quién ha conocido [la] mente [del] Señor, quién {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} instruirá?».
es.B: Porque «¿quién ha conocido jamás la mente del Señor como para darle instrucciones?».
es.R: Las Escrituras preguntan: «¿Quién sabe lo que piensa el Señor? ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} puede enseñar algo?».

vi.L: Vì "ai đã biết tâm trí của Chúa, để dạy bảo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?"
vi.B: Vì "ai đã từng biết tâm trí của Chúa đủ để dạy bảo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?"
vi.R: Kinh Thánh hỏi: "Có ai biết Chúa đang nghĩ gì không? Có ai có thể dạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} điều gì không?"

ko.B: "누가 주님의 마음을 알아서 그분을 가르칠 수 있었느냐?"
ko.R: 성경은 이렇게 묻습니다. "누가 주님의 생각을 알 수 있느냐? 누가 그분에게 무엇을 가르쳐 드릴 수 있느냐?"

decisions.choice: a quotation of Isaiah 40:13, in the form of the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40:12-14 asks who could measure the world or teach God anything. Paul quotes the Greek form of verse 13, as he does in Romans 11:34, without an introduction. Where the Greek has "mind", the Hebrew has "spirit": "Who has measured the Spirit of the LORD?" The Hebrew word fits Paul's subject closely.

decisions.choice: Lord: in Isaiah 40:13 this stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 40:13 the word is the divine name. Here it means God, whose mind no one can know except his Spirit (verse 11). The next sentence then speaks of "the mind of Christ".

decisions.choice: who will instruct him: no one knows the Lord's mind well enough to teach him
decisions.reason: The relative ὃς gives the consequence: who knows God's mind so as to teach him? The expected answer is no one. Verse 15 is not a claim to stand over God.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "the LORD" for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Here Paul quotes the verse with the Greek word "Lord"; meaning decision m2 explains whom it means.

decisions.choice: The Scriptures ask
decisions.reason: Paul does not say he is quoting; Readable tells the reader that these words are from Scripture (m1).

decisions.choice: "ai đã biết tâm trí của Chúa" (L), with "Chúa", not "CHÚA"
decisions.reason: The opening of the Vietnamese Romans 11:34, which quotes the same verse of Isaiah; "Chúa" for the Greek kyrios, as there.

decisions.choice: "주" (L); "주님" (B, R), with no divine_name span; the quotation in 해라체, as in Romans 11:34
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40:13 has the divine name; Paul's Greek has "Lord", which Korean gives as "주" (L) and "주님" (B, R), in the words of Romans 11:34 where Paul quotes the same verse.

records.literal_gloss: We however [the] mind of Christ have.

en.B: But we have the mind of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: But we have been given the mind of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through the Spirit we understand how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} thinks.

fr.L: Mais nous, nous avons la pensée du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Mais nous, nous avons la pensée du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Mais nous, nous avons reçu la pensée du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Par l’Esprit, nous comprenons comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pense.

sw.R: Lakini sisi tumepewa nia ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kupitia Roho tunaelewa jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anavyofikiri.

es.B: Pero nosotros tenemos la mente {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.
es.R: Pero a nosotros se nos ha dado la mente {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Por medio del Espíritu entendemos cómo piensa {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

vi.L: Nhưng chúng ta có tâm trí của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Nhưng chúng ta có tâm trí của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Nhưng chúng ta đã được ban cho tâm trí của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Nhờ Thánh Linh, chúng ta hiểu được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} suy nghĩ thế nào.

ko.R: 그러나 우리는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 마음을 받았습니다. 성령을 통해 우리는 그분이 어떻게 생각하시는지 압니다.

decisions.choice: the mind of Christ: Christ's understanding of God's purposes, his way of thinking, given to believers by the Spirit
alternatives: the mind that thinks like Christ by human effort
decisions.reason: νοῦν is understanding and outlook. Believers do not know everything God knows; they share, through the Spirit (verse 12), Christ's understanding of God's wisdom, the cross included. Compare Philippians 2:5.

decisions.choice: Christ stands where Isaiah has the Lord
decisions.reason: The quotation asked who has known "the mind of the Lord"; Paul answers with "the mind of Christ". He applies to Christ what Isaiah said of the LORD, as he does in 8:6.

decisions.choice: we: those who have received the Spirit from God
decisions.reason: ἡμεῖς is emphatic and takes up "we" of verse 12: by the Spirit, believers have what no natural person has.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: we have been given; through the Spirit we understand how he thinks
decisions.reason: Readable says how believers have Christ's mind and what it means (m1, m3).

decisions.choice: la pensée du Christ, as "la pensée du Seigneur" in the quotation
decisions.reason: The same French word in both halves of the verse keeps the link Paul makes: Christ stands where Isaiah has the Lord (m2). "L'esprit" would be confused with the Spirit.

decisions.choice: nia
decisions.reason: "Nia" (mind, way of thinking) for the Greek word in both halves of verse 16, so the Lord's mind in Isaiah and the mind of Christ stay the same word, as in 1:10.
